method: Timestamps converted to UTC from each page's own publication metadata where retrievable: sina.cn og:published_time; chinanews.com.cn #pubtime_baidu; hkcna.hk on-page time (HKT); oeeee.com article:published_time (+08:00) and JS epoch; bjnews.com.cn on-page time; scmp.com on-page time (HKT). Pages without retrievable metadata (Bloomberg, AP syndication) use GDELT DOC 2.0 'seendate' (first-crawled, 15-min resolution, an upper bound on publication). The Shunde District Health Bureau notice (posted on its WeChat account '健康顺德') has day precision only; it is placed at its latest possible time, i.e. the first page-verified report that quotes it (Sina, 14:49:17 CST). The Hong Kong CHP letter to doctors has day precision (file dated 20250716); placed at 23:59:59 HKT. GDELT queries: 'chikungunya Foshan sourcelang:eng' and 'chikungunya sourcelang:chinese', 2025-07-01..2025-07-28, sort=dateasc, run 2026-09-25. Replay: src/backtest.py sorts items by ts and fires the Sentinel alert at the first item after which >=2 distinct outlets are present AND (an authority item is present OR >=2 languages are present) - the same >=2-independent-source rule as the live Corroborator.
caveats: Lead time is measured from PUBLIC disclosure (Shunde notice, 15 Jul), not from detection: local health authorities detected the cluster on 8 Jul 2025 (China CDC Weekly) and we found no public, timestamped signal before 15 Jul.

The Shunde notice timestamp is derived (day precision; bounded above by the Sina report that quotes it). Strict replay that ignores derived timestamps fires only when the HK CHP letter (English, day precision, placed at 23:59:59 HKT) adds an authority and a second language: 2025-07-16T15:59:59Z -> lead 18.0 h vs SCMP (python3 src/backtest.py --strict).
Chinese-language items largely relay the same official notice; they are distinct outlets, not independent investigations.

'Mainstream' = first English article by a major international outlet that GDELT indexes (SCMP, 17 Jul, a Hong Kong-angle story). Earlier English items outside GDELT's index may exist; we did not find any. Against global wires (Bloomberg 24 Jul, AP 25 Jul) the lead is ~9 days.
Bloomberg and AP timestamps are GDELT first-seen times (15-min resolution, upper bound), not publisher metadata.
The Guangdong CDC repost URL of the Shunde notice returned HTTP 404 on 2026-09-25; the notice text is quoted verbatim in the chinanews.com.cn and cbgc.scol.com.cn reports.
Insured-loss relevance is frequency/A&H/travel/CBI, not a severity cat: all cases mild, no deaths reported; no public insured-loss estimate exists.
